recent_articles.title: Flotilla video: Ben-Gvir’s template of televised abuse was honed on Palestinians | Israel | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Itamar Ben-Gvir**, Israel's national security minister, has been widely criticized for publicly celebrating abuse of detainees in Israeli jails.  He shared a video of the mistreatment of activists intercepted at sea attempting to deliver aid to Gaza, prompting condemnation from numerous countries and even the US ambassador to Israel. While **Benjamin Netanyahu**, the Israeli Prime Minister, condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, he has previously failed to address systemic abuse against Palestinians in custody.  This incident highlights a pattern of escalating violence and human rights violations against Palestinians under his leadership, with calls for sanctions and international intervention growing louder.

recent_articles.title: Bolivia in crisis: Social unrest, demands for president to resign escalate | Protests News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rodrigo Paz**, Bolivia's president, is facing growing social unrest and demands for his resignation.  The protests began over a convergence of sector-based demands, including wage increases, contaminated fuel issues, and land classification changes. **Indigenous groups** from the highlands escalated the protests by blocking roads, demanding the president step down. Former President **Evo Morales**, who was ousted in 2019, has mobilized his supporters to pressure **President Paz**. The government is attempting to address legitimate demands while also cracking down on those deemed hostile to democracy.  The unrest has led to violence and clashes between protesters and police, with over 120 people detained.  **Jose Luis Lupo**, the Presidency Minister, stated that the government will use dialogue for legitimate sectors and full force of the law against those attacking democracy. The situation remains fluid as authorities seek a path forward.

recent_articles.title: Qatar sends mediators to Tehran in sign talks to reopen strait of Hormuz are reaching climax | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Qatar** has dispatched a team of mediators to Tehran in an effort to facilitate talks regarding the Strait of Hormuz. The aim is to sign a memorandum of understanding that would lead to 30 days of discussions on Iran’s nuclear program, deferring discussion of the US demand for the Iranian stockpile of highly enriched uranium. **Marco Rubio**, the US Secretary of State, stated that while some progress has been made, the US will not accept Iran imposing tolls on commercial shipping through the strait.  **Pakistan** is currently considered the main interlocutor for the US in these negotiations.

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse by Israeli forces while detained
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Canadian** Foreign Minister Anita Anand confirmed that her officials have received information detailing the "appalling abuse" of Canadian citizens detained in Israel following the interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. **Germany** and **Spain** also reported injuries among their nationals, while organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla alleged at least 15 cases of sexual assaults and other mistreatment.  The **Israeli** prison service dismissed the allegations as false, stating all detainees were held in accordance with the law.

recent_articles.title: ‘I always hear them before I see them’: Drones strike fear in Colombia | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The use of drones by armed groups in Colombia has significantly increased, posing a serious threat to civilians. The Colombian Ministry of Defence reported 8,395 weaponized drone attacks in 2025, with the number rising sharply from 61 incidents in 2024. These drones are used for both attack and surveillance purposes, enabling armed groups to target infrastructure, police, and the army.  The proliferation of drones has been driven by their affordability and ease of use, allowing groups like the ELN, Clan del Golfo, and FARC dissidents to engage in combat with less risk to themselves. The Colombian government is attempting to counter this threat with anti-drone systems, but armed groups are finding ways around these technologies.  The constant presence of drones has created a climate of fear for civilians, forcing them to live under the constant threat of attack and destruction.

recent_articles.title: Marco Rubio: Trump ‘disappointment’ with Nato will be discussed at summit | Nato | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** expressed disappointment with **Nato allies** for not becoming more actively involved in attacking Iran, setting the stage for a potentially contentious summit. **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, emphasized that the rift would be addressed at the July meeting in Ankara and discussed potential military assistance from **Nato countries** to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if peace talks with Iran fail.  The US is also planning to adjust troop numbers in Europe, although the exact cut remains unclear. Some allies expressed confusion about the White House's erratic policy changes, while others provided limited support for the US attack on Iran.

recent_articles.title: UAE spooked? Fearing Gulf chaos, Abu Dhabi joins Saudis, Qatar in urging Trump against fresh Iran war - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The United Arab Emirates**, **Saudi Arabia**, and **Qatar** have urged US President Donald Trump to avoid restarting military action against Iran and instead pursue diplomacy. These Gulf states are concerned that renewed hostilities could trigger retaliation from Tehran and destabilize the region's economy.  They argue that military action would not achieve Washington’s long-standing objectives with Iran, and they differ on the type of diplomatic arrangement the US should pursue. Despite recent progress in talks between **Iran** and the US, concerns remain about a permanent deal being reached and the potential for renewed conflict if negotiations fail.

recent_articles.title: Why is the US putting pressure on Cuba and what are Trump's aims?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The United States is escalating pressure on Cuba, accusing the country of posing a national security threat and recently indicting former leader Raúl Castro. The US has imposed an oil blockade, sanctions, and a murder indictment against Castro, citing an incident in 1996 where Cuban fighter jets shot down two civilian planes owned by Cuban exiles.  Cuba maintains its actions were justified as self-defense within its airspace and accuses the US of using the charges to justify military aggression. The US has also targeted senior Cuban officials accused of human rights abuses or corruption, while offering $100 million in aid through humanitarian organizations. Cuba's response has been characterized by fiery rhetoric, with leaders demanding an end to the blockade and accusing the US of "coercion" and threats. China and Russia have condemned the US pressure on Cuba.

recent_articles.title: Czech president urges Nato to ‘show its teeth’ over Russia’s provocations | Nato | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Petr Pavel**, the Czech president, urged **NATO** to take a more assertive stance against Russia's provocations.  He suggested various measures like cutting off Russian banks from global financial systems and shooting down violating aircraft. Pavel emphasized the need for decisive responses to deter further aggression by Moscow, citing Russia's disregard for diplomatic solutions and its willingness to escalate tensions. He also called for increased pressure on **Russia** from the United States, particularly through tougher sanctions tied to a potential peace settlement in Ukraine.  Despite domestic disagreements with the Czech government, Pavel remains committed to pushing **NATO** forward on this issue.

recent_articles.title: Rubio's maiden India visit aims to repair strained ties; boost Quad cooperation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio** will visit **India** from May 23 to 26, 2026, aiming to repair strained bilateral ties.  He will meet with **External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and attend a Quad Foreign Ministers meeting in New Delhi. The trip follows a recent three-day visit by **India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri** to Washington DC focused on stabilizing the relationship.  The talks are expected to focus on bolstering ties in energy, trade, investment, critical technology, and people-to-people exchanges, as well as discussing the West Asia crisis and its economic impact.

recent_articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump's top US intelligence official - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tulsi Gabbard** resigned as President Donald Trump's director of national intelligence, citing her husband's diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer. She informed **Trump** during an Oval Office meeting on Friday and the resignation is effective June 30th.  **Aaron Lukas**, the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, will serve as acting director while Gabbard focuses on supporting her husband.
